q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
report:
Yes on the raw numbers: comparing games on the same network, smaller crowds went with smaller national TV audiences (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62). Mostly no after comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result: the correlation falls to 0.16 in 2025 (range -0.05 to 0.37) and 0.14 in 2026 (range -0.08 to 0.34), and both ranges include zero. (table: crowd_tv_headline) In 2025, ESPN had 26 games with a crowd-to-audience correlation of 0.49 (range 0.13 to 0.74) and a correlation of 0.27 (range -0.14 to 0.59) after adjusting for each park's usual crowd, while FS1 had 34 games with a correlation of 0.29 (range -0.05 to 0.57) and an adjusted correlation of 0.17 (range -0.18 to 0.48), and TBS had 22 games with a correlation of 0.40 (range -0.02 to 0.71) and an adjusted correlation of 0.08 (range -0.35 to 0.48) (table: crowd_tv_residual). In 2026, ESPN had 23 games with a crowd-to-audience correlation of 0.48 (range 0.08 to 0.74) and an adjusted correlation of 0.30 (range -0.12 to 0.64), FS1 had 21 games with a correlation of 0.52 (range 0.12 to 0.78) and an adjusted correlation of 0.43 (range -0.01 to 0.72), NBC had 21 games with a correlation of 0.56 (range 0.17 to 0.80) and an adjusted correlation of -0.08 (range -0.49 to 0.37), and TBS had 10 games with a correlation of 0.65 (range 0.04 to 0.91) and an adjusted correlation of -0.58 (range -0.89 to 0.07) (table: crowd_tv_residual).

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like. These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: What was the attendance at the Speedway Classic?
report:
The Speedway Classic on August 2, 2025, between the Cincinnati Reds and Atlanta Braves drew an attendance of 91,032 (table: games). This historic matchup was the first regular-season National League or American League game played in the state of Tennessee and the first MLB game played on a racetrack ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)). The crowd of 91,032 coincided with a new all-time regular-season MLB attendance record, hosted within the massive 146,000-seat Bristol Motor Speedway NASCAR venue ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)). This record-setting turnout also coincided with prominent pregame entertainment, including a headline concert by Tim McGraw, Pitbull, and Jake Owen, plus an outdoor fan zone with a 110-foot Ferris wheel ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)).

q: What drives MLB attendance?
report:
MLB attendance is strongest for home openers, weekend games, and matchups against high-profile opponents like the Los Angeles Dodgers. At the team level, a season win rate that is .100 higher coincides with an 8.6% increase in expected attendance, while a 10% higher crowd over the prior two years relates to an 8.2% increase (table: model_coefficients). A 10% larger metro population has a negligible 0.2% effect that is not clear (table: model_coefficients). For individual games, home openers see a massive 69.1% boost in attendance (table: model_coefficients). Playing the Los Angeles Dodgers coincides with a 25.0% jump, followed by the New York Yankees at 15.7%, the Chicago Cubs at 13.1%, the Philadelphia Phillies at 9.5%, and the Boston Red Sox at 5.2% (table: model_coefficients). Conversely, falling behind in the standings hurts crowds, with each game further behind the division leader reducing attendance by 0.3% (table: model_coefficients). Timing and weather also play major roles. Compared to Fridays, Saturday games see an 8.8% increase, while Mondays drop by 21.8%, Wednesdays by 20.6%, Tuesdays by 18.9%, and Thursdays by 16.6% (table: model_coefficients). Sunday games show a minor, unclear decrease of 1.0% (table: model_coefficients). By month, compared to August, July games are up 4.2% and June games are up 2.5%, while March and April games are down 10.9% and May games are down 3.1% (table: model_coefficients). Bad weather like rain, drizzle, or snow goes with a 5.7% drop, and playing under a closed roof or dome relates to a 7.0% decrease (table: model_coefficients).

*These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: How did the Cubs do on attendance and viewership last year?
report:
During the 2025 season, the Chicago Cubs grew their home attendance to an average of 37,130 fans per game while averaging 1,030,818 viewers for their single-game national television broadcasts (table: team_season_model) (table: team_tv_summary). On television, the Cubs made 17 national appearances, including 12 single games, 5 Fox window games, and 2 special event games (table: team_tv_summary). Their single-game broadcasts peaked at 2,041,000 viewers, with a network mix of 6 games on Fox, 5 on ESPN, 3 on FS1, and 3 on TBS (table: team_tv_summary).

q: Did the Red Sox or the Yankees have better season opener attendance in 2024?
report: The New York Yankees had higher attendance for their 2024 home opener than the Boston Red Sox, though the Red Sox played in front of a larger crowd for the very first game of the regular season (table: games_clean).
